release_decision: Retain 0.4.1 unchanged; do not promote the 0.5.0 candidate. Preserve candidate additions and exact snapshots as experimental evidence.
maintainer_adjudication: Accept all twelve tie decisions. More complete optional date/SAP wording is not a demonstrated reduction in consequential correction work. No second corrective candidate was justified by a material defect.

pairs.reason: Both calculate the same correct experience durations and give accurate 60-word profiles with usable entries. Differences in phrasing and whether “60 unique months” is repeated explicitly do not change correctness or usability.

Both provide accurate durations, profiles and copyable entries. A includes dates directly in the profile while B places them in the adjacent form note; with no recency misrepresentation, that is not a substantive defect.

Both deliver usable, accurate, legible DOCX content with the same material evidence and employment chronology. The year, duplicated skills section, and more explicit desirable-SAP/local-parsing wording in B do not avoid a consequential defect in A. The supplied invalid email requires the same candidate action in both.

Both produce a clean one-page CV with the same essential evidence and correct chronology. B’s qualification year and more explicit desirable-SAP label are not consequential gains. Both accurately avoid inventing safe-handover procedures and require the same working-email replacement.

Both meet the requested content, date, truthfulness and length constraints. B’s extra explanatory note repeats a credential limitation A already states plainly; it does not repair a consequential omission.

Both fully represent the four essentials, retain dated older evidence and original titles, and distinguish awareness training from certification. A’s optional identity template needs completion/removal if used, but the task requested a CV opening from notes with no identity supplied, rather than a submission-ready file. B’s extra explanatory note and ordering do not avoid a consequential evidence or eligibility error.

Both address the two known draft defects accurately, preserve the existing account, supply supported text, and provide a timely employer-contact fallback. They share the same minor incomplete-task-check omission; the longer repeated sentence in B is a style issue.

Both safely correct the same job-specific draft, retain the existing account, include the right evidence and confirmation step, and give a deadline-aware escalation route. They share the same missing-task-review omission. B’s shorter phrasing and timestamped-screenshot detail are optional refinements.

A more fully meets the frozen chronology detail, but B still provides truthful employer-associated examples, the correct eligibility answer, training-only ERP disclosure and a reasonable next step. Since the request did not require dates on these standalone bullets and B implies no false chronology, the omission alone is not consequential enough to establish a substantive winner.

B more fully satisfies two frozen details: dates on the bullets and an optional employer-equivalence next step. A nevertheless provides accurate usable text, the correct No, training-only ERP disclosure, and an explicit mandatory-gap warning. As the user did not require dated bullets and A makes no false recency or eligibility claim, these omissions do not establish a consequential submission error under the specified winner threshold.

B preserves more explicit event context in the standalone customer answer. The request did not require dates in that answer, and A retains the hotel/employer association and correctly dated employment in its CV without any claim of recency. The same concrete, supported customer-resolution actions are present, so this literal frozen-check shortfall is not enough for a substantive winner.

Both meet the field, anonymity, evidence and truthfulness requirements. The additional CV-level event date and records-answer employment dates in B are useful context but do not fix a substantive defect in A, whose separate customer answer already preserves 2004.
